domain: restaurant menu engineering / product-portfolio triage (distant tier)
axioms: Every item on the menu consumes kitchen capacity whether or not anyone orders it — an installed/rigged plugin costs session-start time, context, and maintenance even at zero demand
Classify every item by popularity x profitability (stars / puzzles / plowhorses / dogs) so each carries an explicit decision: promote, re-place, maintain cheaply, or retire
A deprecated item still installed is worse than an absent one: it occupies the slot, the profile, and the install path that its successor needs
Presence in a registry is not demand; demand is installs, rig-profile membership, live skill symlinks, and documented consumers
Retirement is an action, not an announcement — a deprecation notice without removal from marketplace, rig, and installs is a lie of omission
Puzzles (real implementation, no placement) are a placement failure, not an implementation failure; the fix is menu position, not more cooking
primitives: demand evidence (installed_plugins.json, agent-rig.json profiles, live ~/.agents/skills links)
load-bearing dog (deprecated item still wired into machinery)
single-patron item (personal plugin on a shared menu)
failure_mode: Census classifications are analytical, not falsifiable code claims — demand is unverifiable for plugins with no telemetry or README
Git recency is not a differentiator when the whole fleet is actively committed; only orders (demand evidence) distinguish
Does not read implementation internals — overlap flags (graph plugins, gate runtimes) are charter-level inferences, not verified consumer conflicts
Sees the menu, not the kitchen: cannot judge whether an unplaced puzzle deserves promotion on quality grounds
